candidate.answerReason: Adding the sum and difference equations gives twice the larger number, 26. The larger number is 13 and the smaller is 7.

methods.label: Model the sum and difference
methods.explanation: Let the larger number be \(x\) and the smaller number be \(y\): \(x+y=20\), \(x-y=6\). Adding gives \(2x=26\), so \(x=13\), \(y=7\).
methods.levelReason: Modeling the two relationships and adding the equations are within Grade 7.

methods.label: Equalize the numbers
methods.explanation:
Subtracting \(6\) from the larger number makes it equal to the smaller number. Their total is now \(20-6\), made up of two copies of the smaller number. Thus the smaller number is
\[
(20-6)\div2=7.
\]
Adding back the difference gives the larger number, \(7+6=13\). The answer is \(13,7\).
methods.levelReason: Equalizing the numbers uses only elementary whole-number arithmetic, below the stated Grade 7 scope.
